lines.text: Lesson ten: a tour of an exchange platform. Let's learn the screen, one piece at a time.
lines.say: Lesson ten: a tour of an exchange platform. Let's learn the screen, one piece at a time.

lines.text: Open any trading app and you'll see a screen like this. So many boxes!
lines.say: Open any trading app and you'll see a screen like this. So many boxes!

lines.text: This is an educational mock, not a real exchange screen. Real apps look different and change often.
lines.say: This is an educational mock, not a real exchange screen. Real apps look different and change often.

lines.text: But they share the same few parts.
lines.say: But they share the same few parts.

lines.text: Think of it like a car dashboard. Each part has one job.
lines.say: Think of it like a car dashboard. Each part has one job.

lines.text: Watchlist, symbol bar and chart. Order book and order entry.
lines.say: Watchlist, symbol bar and chart. Order book and order entry.

lines.text: Positions at the bottom, and your wallet and security up top.
lines.say: Positions at the bottom, and your wallet and security up top.

lines.text: We'll visit each one. No real orders, no real money.
lines.say: We'll visit each one. No real orders, no real money.

lines.text: First, the watchlist. It's a list of trading pairs you want to keep an eye on.
lines.say: First, the watchlist. It's a list of trading pairs you want to keep an eye on.

lines.text: Type BTC in the search box, and the list narrows to Bitcoin.
lines.say: Type B-T-C in the search box, and the list narrows to Bitcoin.

lines.text: Tap BTC/USDT, and the whole screen switches to that pair.
lines.say: Tap B-T-C U-S-D-T, and the whole screen switches to that pair.

lines.text: Up top is the symbol bar. A symbol is the short name of a market, like BTCUSDT.
lines.say: Up top is the symbol bar. A symbol is the short name of a market, like B-T-C U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Next to it: the last traded price, and the change over the past 24 hours.
lines.say: Next to it: the last traded price, and the change over the past twenty-four hours.

lines.text: Example: 24 hours ago, 60,000. Now 61,200. That's up 1,200 USDT, or +2%.
lines.say: Example: twenty-four hours ago, sixty thousand. Now sixty-one thousand two hundred. That's up one thousand two hundred U-S-D-T, or plus two percent.

lines.text: The chart shows price over time. Each candle covers one slice of time, like one minute.
lines.say: The chart shows price over time. Each candle covers one slice of time, like one minute.

lines.text: Watch the newest candle form. It grows as trades happen at new prices.
lines.say: Watch the newest candle form. It grows as trades happen at new prices.

lines.text: Tabs like 1m, 5m and 15m change the time slice. T14 and T15 cover this.
lines.say: Tabs like one-minute, five-minute and fifteen-minute change the time slice. T fourteen and T fifteen cover this.

lines.text: The order book lists waiting orders: sellers' asks on top, buyers' bids below.
lines.say: The order book lists waiting orders: sellers' asks on top, buyers' bids below.

lines.text: The gap between the best ask and the best bid is the spread. Here: 60,010 − 60,000 = 10 USDT.
lines.say: The gap between the best ask and the best bid is the spread. Here: sixty thousand ten minus sixty thousand equals ten U-S-D-T.

lines.text: When a market buy arrives, it takes the best ask, and the last price ticks up.
lines.say: When a market buy arrives, it takes the best ask, and the last price ticks up.

lines.text: The order entry panel is where an order is set up. Choose a type: limit, market or stop.
lines.say: The order entry panel is where an order is set up. Choose a type: limit, market or stop.

lines.text: Enter a price and a size. Say a limit buy at 60,000 for 0.010 BTC.
lines.say: Enter a price and a size. Say a limit buy at sixty thousand for zero point zero one B-T-C.

lines.text: Order value is price × size: 60,000 × 0.010 = 600 USDT. The fee estimate shows too.
lines.say: Order value is price times size: sixty thousand times zero point zero one equals six hundred U-S-D-T. The fee estimate shows too.

lines.text: Here the buttons are mock only. No real order is sent.
lines.say: Here the buttons are mock only. No real order is sent.

lines.text: Once an order fills, it becomes a position, listed at the bottom of the screen.
lines.say: Once an order fills, it becomes a position, listed at the bottom of the screen.

lines.text: PnL means profit and loss. Unrealized PnL is your result so far, on an open position.
lines.say: P and L means profit and loss. Unrealized P and L is your result so far, on an open position.

lines.text: Long 0.010 BTC from 60,000. Price 60,600: +6 USDT. Price 59,400: −6 USDT.
lines.say: Long zero point zero one B-T-C from sixty thousand. Price sixty thousand six hundred: plus six U-S-D-T. Price fifty-nine thousand four hundred: minus six U-S-D-T.

lines.text: It's only realized when you close the position.
lines.say: It's only realized when you close the position.

lines.text: Your wallet shows the money in your account. Here, a fictional 1,000 USDT.
lines.say: Your wallet shows the money in your account. Here, a fictional one thousand U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Part of it is in use, held for open orders and positions. The rest is available.
lines.say: Part of it is in use, held for open orders and positions. The rest is available.

lines.text: Example: 1,000 − 600 in use = 400 USDT available for new orders.
lines.say: Example: one thousand minus six hundred in use equals four hundred U-S-D-T available for new orders.

lines.text: Last stop: security settings. They protect your account.
lines.say: Last stop: security settings. They protect your account.

lines.text: Two-factor login asks for a second code from your phone, as well as your password.
lines.say: Two-factor login asks for a second code from your phone, as well as your password.

lines.text: An anti-phishing code appears in real emails from the exchange, so fakes stand out.
lines.say: An anti-phishing code appears in real emails from the exchange, so fakes stand out.

lines.text: API keys let software use your account. Never share them, or any code. XORA never asks.
lines.say: A-P-I keys let software use your account. Never share them, or any code. Zora never asks.

lines.text: A common mistake: learning where the buttons sit, instead of what they say.
lines.say: A common mistake: learning where the buttons sit, instead of what they say.

lines.text: Apps update. Here, an update swaps the buttons. A tap from memory hits Sell, not Buy.
lines.say: Apps update. Here, an update swaps the buttons. A tap from memory hits Sell, not Buy.

lines.text: Correction: always read the label, and check the order before you confirm.
lines.say: Correction: always read the label, and check the order before you confirm.

lines.text: Your turn. Where would you look to see your unrealized PnL? Pause if you need more time.
lines.say: Your turn. Where would you look to see your unrealized P and L? Pause if you need more time.

lines.text: The answer is C, the positions panel. It shows your open positions and their PnL.
lines.say: The answer is C, the positions panel. It shows your open positions and their P and L.

lines.text: Not A, the chart. The chart shows the market price, not your own result.
lines.say: Not A, the chart. The chart shows the market price, not your own result.

lines.text: First, some safety rules for real apps.
lines.say: First, some safety rules for real apps.

lines.text: Check the address. A look-alike website can steal your login.
lines.say: Check the address. A look-alike website can steal your login.

lines.text: Check which market you're in, spot or futures, before any order.
lines.say: Check which market you're in, spot or futures, before any order.

lines.text: Never tap around a real account to explore. A tap can place a real order.
lines.say: Never tap around a real account to explore. A tap can place a real order.

lines.text: And WAIT, or no trade, is always a valid choice.
lines.say: And wait, or no trade, is always a valid choice.

lines.text: Every trading screen is built from the same parts, each with one job.
lines.say: Every trading screen is built from the same parts, each with one job.

lines.text: Positions show your unrealized PnL. The wallet shows what's still available.
lines.say: Positions show your unrealized P and L. The wallet shows what's still available.

lines.text: Read every label, protect your account, and never share keys or codes.
lines.say: Read every label, protect your account, and never share keys or codes.

lines.text: Check yourself: where do you find the spread?
lines.say: Check yourself: where do you find the spread?

lines.text: In the order book: the gap between the best ask and the best bid.
lines.say: In the order book: the gap between the best ask and the best bid.

lines.text: Great work! Next up, T11: spot versus futures. What do you really own?
lines.say: Great work! Next up, T eleven: spot versus futures. What do you really own?
